failures.message: ran and passed with its mutant applied to saffron/ledger.py — `finish_run` writes `COMPLETE` or `ABORTED`, and refuses every other status with `ValueError` before it writes. A refused call leaves the run's row `RUNNING` with no `ended_at`, and appends no `run_finished` fact. The witness drives a run holding a task and a run holding none, on a fresh ledger with a record. It also drives a ledger whose `runs` table is the home ledger's own, with no `CHECK`. The refused statuses are the misspelling `ABORTD`, a lower-case `complete`, `RUNNING`, the preflight outcomes `PASSED` and `FAILED`, the batch stop reason `DRAINED` and the empty string. On that older ledger, an existing row holding NULL and one holding a status outside the set read as they did before the ledger opened. (untested case: an admitted status other than COMPLETE written as handed)

ran and passed with its mutant applied to saffron/ledger.py — `fold_task` raises `ValueError` on a `run_finished` fact whose status is not `COMPLETE` or `ABORTED`, and the ledger then holds no row for that task. The witness reads a task's facts after `finish_run` closed its run `ABORTED`. It swaps that fact's status for `ABORTD`, `complete`, `RUNNING`, the preflight outcomes `PASSED` and `FAILED`, the batch stop reason `DRAINED` and the empty string in turn. It folds each into a fresh ledger and into a ledger whose `runs` table is the home ledger's own, with no `CHECK`. It reads the task's rows after each refused fold. (untested case: a run_finished fact folding an admitted status other than COMPLETE)
